explanation: Yen means 'round object' or 'circle'. China's yuan and Korea's won come from the same Chinese character, a reminder of the round silver coins once traded across East Asia.

claims.text: Japan's Meiji government introduced the yen in 1871.
The won, the yuan and the baht are the currencies of Korea, China and Thailand, not Japan.
Yen means 'round object' or 'circle' in Japanese.
The names yen, yuan and won all come from the same Chinese character, meaning round.
The name refers to round coins, especially the silver coins traded across East Asia in the 19th century.
